title: S(3;5,6,8) = 183
statement: The generalized off-diagonal Schur number S(3;5,6,8) is exactly 183: every 3-colouring of {1,...,183} contains x_1+...+x_{4}=x_5 monochromatic in colour 1, or x_1+...+x_{5}=x_6 monochromatic in colour 2, or x_1+...+x_{7}=x_8 monochromatic in colour 3; and some 3-colouring of {1,...,182} avoids all three.

provenance.conjectured_by: Ahmed-Schaal Conjecture 2 predicts S(3;s,t,u) = s*t*u - t*u - u - 1 for 4 <= s <= t <= u. This value, 183, AGREES with it. The conjecture is open; arXiv:2604.11030 (Song and Mao, April 2026) proves the companion Conjecture 1 but not this one.

The deciding CNF is the SUBSUMPTION-MINIMAL encoding: for solution sets S subset of S', clause(S) implies clause(S'), so only the minimal antichain is emitted -- a SUBSET of the full clause list, so refuting it refutes the full instance. check-claim-certificates.py validates the stored CNF clause by clause rather than by byte-identity, which is the check the bound actually needs. The deciding CNF is NOT stored beside this claim (49422096 bytes gzipped); there is therefore no instance-pin row, and check-claim-certificates.py reports this row as NOT re-checked here rather than passing it. notes: NEW VALUE. NEW VALUE: not among Ahmed-Schaal's eleven exact values and not in Song-Mao arXiv:2604.11030 Table 3. The lower bound was a theorem; the upper bound is established here. Generated by crates/axeyum-search/src/offdiag.rs entry point OffDiagonalSchur::minimal_problem. Both sides are discharged -- n = N-1 satisfiable with an independently replayed colouring, n = N refuted with a DRAT proof re-derived by axeyum's own checker. SOUNDNESS NOTE: colours here are NOT interchangeable (each forbids a different equation), so the usual whole-palette symmetry breaking is UNSOUND and would produce a wrong unsat. The encoding orders colour classes only within blocks of colours carrying the SAME equation, and crates/axeyum-search/tests/offdiag_schur.rs carries a negative control showing the unblocked version turning satisfiable S(3;3,4,5) at n=41 into unsat.
